data.narrative:
Synhelion, a Series C climate and energy technology company, has raised $80M+ to date. The valuation assessment draws on a peer set of 3 same-stage, same-sector comparables (KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy) with a broader climate tech universe that includes 1 public company and 8 private peers.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $80M total raised as a proxy base and applies a 1.7x multiplier typical for Series C advancement, yielding $136M. Peer-median analysis anchors to the median valuation of the 3-company comp set at $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B, reflecting material dispersion in how the market values climate tech companies at this stage.

Triangulating these two methods produces a range of $116M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $568M. The wide spread reflects uncertainty inherent in early-stage deep tech valuation, where peer comparables trade at valuations spanning 4x, and stage-progression methods rely on proxies rather than disclosed financials. The median point ($568M) sits materially above stage-progression but below peer median, suggesting the company occupies a mid-range position relative to named competitors. Key uncertainties include technology maturation risk, capital intensity to commercialization, and whether peer valuations reflect sustainable market pricing or temporary capital abundance in the climate tech sector.
